Class DiaryUserInterface

java.lang.Object
edu.ntnu.idi.bidata.DiaryUserInterface
public class DiaryUserInterface extends Object
The DiaryUserInterface class represents the text-based user interface of the diary application.

Role and Responsibility

This class is responsible for controlling program flow, handling all user input, validating that input, and delegating requests to underlying registers such as UserRegister and DiaryEntryRegister.

Key-Responsibilities:

This class acts as the bridge between the user and the core application logic. It is responsible for:

  • User login and registration
  • Creating, editing, and deleting diary entries
  • Displaying menus and steering the application’s control flow
  • Validating all types of input (text, integers, dates)
  • Performing searches (by date, date range, keyword)
  • Ensuring correct access control based on the currently logged-in user
  • Loading and saving persistent data via JSON through the register classes
Information Stored and Data Type Justification
  • The registry of users (UserRegister): Manages all user-related operations. Using a dedicated register class separates user management concerns from UI logic.
  • The reistry of diary entries (DiaryEntryRegister): Manages all diary entry operations. By seperating the the management of the diary entries from the UI, it allows for a cleaner code organising.
  • The current user (currentUser): Tracks the currently logged-in user by using a User reference. This allows for direct access to the users author object. If the currentUser holds the value null it indicates that no user is currently logged in.
Mutability Assessment

The userRegister and the diaryEntryRegister is set at creation. These two are final and wont be changed. The currentUser is also set at creation to the value null. It will later be changed when a user logges in to the application.

Invalid Data Handling Strategy

This class is the primarely line of defence against invalid input. It users input validation using retry loops

Inspiration

This class takes some inspiration from Tri Tac Le's repository NTNU-IDI/idatt1003-mappe-del-1-2024-TriTacLeidatt1003-mappe-del-1-2024-TriTacLe in the design of the two methods runMainMenu(Scanner scan) and start(Scanner scan)
